title: Demo Session: Token Auth Service (2-file Sandbox)
description: Zero-token deterministic replay session illustrating cross-file AST chunks, Chalk Marks, split-screen /explain tours, /edge warnings, and /test mocking.

chunk.summary: Define UserRole, AuthUser, and AuthResult domain contracts.

tourSteps.explanationMarkdown: `AuthUser` keeps authentication state minimal: `id`, `email`, `role`, and an optional `suspended` flag so downstream authorization checks don't need extra DB columns.
`AuthResult.reason` enumerates the four explicit failure modes instead of free-form error strings, making HTTP status mapping deterministic.

chunks.edgeNotes: Watch `expiresAtMs` across distributed nodes — if servers have clock skew, tokens near expiry could intermittently pass or fail.

chunk.summary: Add AuthService class shell with token verification store dependency.

tourSteps.explanationMarkdown: `TokenStore` decouples storage lookups from business rules. Notice in the split pane how `SessionToken` carries `expiresAtMs` so `AuthService` can validate expiry purely in memory.
Injecting `now: () => number = () => Date.now()` lets tests freeze time cleanly without monkey-patching globals.

edgeMarks.label: Sync TokenStore won't fit async DBs without Promise<>

chunks.edgeNotes: If `TokenStore` later talks to Redis or Postgres, these methods will need to become async (`Promise<...>`).

chunk.summary: Implement authorize(rawToken, requiredRole) with expiry, suspension, and role hierarchy checks.

tourSteps.explanationMarkdown: We reject blank tokens first, then look up the session and compare `expiresAtMs <= this.now()`. Returning `{ ok: false, reason: 'expired' }` for both unknown and expired tokens avoids leaking whether a token ever existed.
Mapping `UserRole` to a typed `Record<UserRole, number>` means TypeScript forces us to update the rank table if a new role is ever added in `userTypes.ts`.

edgeMarks.label: Non-constant-time token lookup if store uses naive string compare

chunks.edgeNotes: Two subtle edge cases: (1) `!user` collapses deleted users into `reason: 'suspended'`, and (2) make sure `TokenStore.findToken` uses hashed/indexed lookup rather than naive plaintext comparison.
